solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: WASHINGTON POST? It's full of them

parts.note: Washington is the US seat of government, a national capital
post is mail, which consists of letters

explanation.surface: A comment on the American newspaper being packed with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the clue itself: the masthead is printed entirely in upper case.
explanation.definitionFit: The two printed words, shown in upper case, are made up entirely of big characters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Gas cooker not approved by the Queen

parts.words: cooker not approved by the Queen
parts.note: take the word cooker, remove OK (approved) and ER (the Queen), leaving C and O, the chemical formula of this gas

explanation.surface: A gas oven that lacks a royal seal of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: COOKER minus OK ('approved') and ER ('the Queen') leaves CO, the chemical formula for the gas, which the solver must then name. Gas appliances that burn badly really do give it off.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound of one carbon and one oxygen atom is a colourless, poisonous gas.

clue.text: Leaves on this, having intention to be in Paris by start of evening

parts.note: an intention is a plan
être is French for 'to be'

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: Someone intends to be in Paris by early evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about departing, but it is a noun: the foliage on this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a broad-leaved tree, so foliage grows on it; the definition describes it loosely.

clue.text: Prove attractive to couple wanting top personal trainer

indicators.note: wanting top means the word for couple loses its first letter, which is the top in a down entry

parts.note: a couple in a relationship is called an item

explanation.surface: A couple manage without the best fitness coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prove attractive to' is a verb phrase, and the answer is a verb: lure or entice.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to be attractive enough that they are drawn in.

clue.text: Rakish French composer standing in queue?

indicators.note: standing in places the composer's name within the word for queue

parts.note: a queue is a line
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: A dissolute French composer waiting in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dissolute and unrestrained, and as an adjective libertine means the same.

clue.text: See 1
Fast car? Boorish males have an increasingly high time …

indicators.note: increasingly high says the letter for time climbs further up the down entry

parts.note: louts are boorish men

explanation.surface: Uncouth men in a speedy car get progressively more intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'high' means nearer the top: the T in LOUTS moves up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a British maker of sports cars, so one is an example of a quick motor.

clue.text: … on the other hand, hen night gets abandoned with one hour gone and AA brought in

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged
gone says that one letter is removed from the phrase hen night

parts.note: one hour is a single H, the abbreviation for hour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bachelorette party is called off, and Alcoholics Anonymous gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' takes one H from HEN NIGHT; 'brought in' adds AA to the pool, and 'abandoned' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a contrasting consideration, an idiomatic equivalent of 'however'.

clue.text: One using mic regularly?

parts.note: a master of ceremonies speaks into a microphone often; also the regular letters M and C of mic spell the abbreviation said this way

explanation.surface: A question about who habitually holds a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the spelt-out pronunciation of MC, and taking every other letter of 'mic' gives M and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère or host introduces acts through a microphone as part of the job.

clue.text: Part which young children learn in school play

parts.note: to part is to separate, as a verb

parts.words: which young children learn in school
parts.note: pupils learn multiplication tables at primary school

explanation.surface: A role that small pupils learn for a school drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' and 'play' suggest acting; 'play' is the definition, a Terence Rattigan drama of 1954.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate Tables is a pair of one-act plays by the English dramatist Terence Rattigan.

clue.text: Area in football club closing at end of first half

indicators.text: closing at end of first half
indicators.note: closing at the end of the first half keeps only the opening half of the club's name, its first five of ten letters

parts.note: Real Madrid is a Spanish football club

explanation.surface: A region inside a football club, with the game shut down at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Real Madrid has ten letters; keep only the first five.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field, such as an area of study or a kingdom's territory.

clue.text: Flower putting scent, say, into soft soap

indicators.note: putting with into tells us one piece is placed inside another
into names the phrase for soft soap as the container

parts.note: to soft-soap someone is to flatter, or butter up
scent sounds like cent, abbreviated C

explanation.surface: Someone adds perfume to a gentle cleaning product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the sound: scent is heard as cent, a coin abbreviated C, which goes inside BUTTER UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of meadows.

clue.text: Spills from open vessels

parts.note: overt means open, done publicly
urns are vessels

explanation.surface: Liquid sloshing out of uncovered containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spills' reads as a noun for spillage; it is a verb, tips over.
explanation.definitionFit: To spill something is to upset or tip it over, as when knocking a glass.

clue.text: Prince of foreign 9 using euro, originally in place of pound

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged
in place of says one letter substitutes for another

parts.note: the solution to 9 across
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word euro

explanation.surface: A prince of a foreign kingdom switching from sterling to the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: In REALM, E replaces L to give REAME, which 'foreign' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Device for inputting chart? Small chart in ICT setting

parts.note: a chart is a graph

indicators.note: in tells us the small chart goes within ICT
setting says ICT surrounds the other pieces, like a mount for a jewel

parts.note: taken as written; ICT is information and communications technology
a table is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gadget enters diagrams, then describing a little chart in computing class.
explanation.walkthrough: ICT is the UK school name for computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing pad with a stylus feeds hand-drawn input into a computer.

clue.text: Chat-up line is one primarily about essential oil

indicators.note: about means around in a jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letters of line, is and one

explanation.surface: A pick-up line that is chiefly about perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli oil is a fragrant extract from an Asian plant, used in perfumes.

clue.text: Plant produced from seed that's hard to prune

parts.note: a stone is the hard seed of a fruit such as a plum
to prune is to crop or cut back

explanation.surface: A plant grown from a tough seed that is hard to cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prune' suggests the dried plum, near 'seed'; here it is the verb, to crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a succulent sedum growing on walls and rocks.

clue.text: Sugar briefly loses value when cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged
briefly says the word loses is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sugar loses some of its worth when heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims LOSES to LOSE before the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Laevulose is an old name for fructose, the fruit sugar.

clue.text: See 1
Public house emptied out, to combat one way of obtaining drugs

parts.note: overt means public, not hidden

indicators.note: emptied out leaves only the outside letters of the word house

parts.note: to counter is to combat

explanation.surface: A pub is cleared to fight against one route to getting drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public house' looks like a pub, but 'Public' and 'house' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines sold without a prescription are bought across the shop counter.

clue.text: See 8
Appeal with some vigour when opener one short of a ton?

indicators.note: opener names the first figure of the hundred as the one dropped
short of says that leading figure goes missing

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, written in digits as one, zero, zero, read here as letters
the digit one looks like the letter I
mph, miles per hour, measures speed, a sign of vigour; a ton is also 100 mph

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the top of the order on ninety-nine makes a lively appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' and 'ton' suggest cricket; a ton is 100, and dropping the leading 1 leaves zeros read as O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph means energetic attractiveness, the allure some people have.

clue.text: Half-hearted 7, given revised opening fight

indicators.note: half-hearted halves the heart: the central Roman C, a hundred, becomes L, fifty
revised opening says the first two letters of the word are swapped round

parts.note: the solution to 7 down

explanation.surface: A lukewarm compère, given a new intro, starts a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised opening' turns EM into ME; the middle letter C (100 in Roman numerals) is halved to L (50).
explanation.definitionFit: A mêlée is a confused scuffle or brawl involving many people.

clue.text: Misplace tabulation partly showing depressions in hip area

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Mislaying a table of figures partly reveals hollows in the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: The acetabulum is the cup-shaped socket in the pelvis where the thigh bone sits.

clue.text: In the middle of stewing mango

indicators.note: stewing cooks and churns the fruit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is busy cooking a tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means surrounded by, as in standing amid a crowd.

clue.text: Lost some of what's earnings-related

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Confusion about part of something tied to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bewildered or adrift is idiomatically described as being out on the ocean.

clue.text: Bad mood caused by sick joke?

parts.note: sick means ill
a joke shows humour

explanation.surface: A tasteless gag puts someone in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick joke' reads as one dark gag; split it into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is grumpiness, an old phrase for a sour temper.

clue.text: Swimming group that's also hard- working

indicators.note: working means fermenting or in motion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A team of swimmers who are diligent too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard-working' looks like one adjective; 'hard' gives H and 'working' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a large group of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Fiancée oddly no longer angry vespers cut out these?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so all the letters are rearranged
oddly no longer drops the odd-numbered letters of the word, keeping the even ones

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut says the word vespers is trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fiancée, calmer now, scraps the evening church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiancée without its odd letters gives INE; 'cut' trims VESPERS to VESPER; 'out' rearranges these with ANGRY. 'these' points back at vespers, which are such services.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening service of devotions, so 'these' refers to the clue's own word.
